questions.title: Which dashboard screen do you want?
questions.explanation: A larger center screen replaces the smaller screen; these are separate installed systems, not two screens in one dashboard.
questions.availability: Tradesman starts with the 8.4-inch screen shown in R12546. The 12-inch screen is optional on Express, an H2 package option on Big Horn/Lone Star, and standard on Laramie. The larger UBW system is optional with applicable Laramie, Rebel, Limited and Longhorn packages and standard on Tungsten. The factory chart calls UBW 14.5 inches; the manufacturer bulletin identifies UBW as 14.4 inches, matching the pictured R12315 sticker. Inventory matching keeps each vehicle’s exact sticker size.

questions.title: Which front-seat configuration do you want?
questions.explanation: Tradesman starts with a vinyl split bench. These photos show specific bucket-seat upgrades. Deluxe cloth and leather-trimmed buckets include power driver adjustment; selecting that seat configuration also affects your next choices.
questions.availability: Tradesman starts with vinyl 40/20/40 split-bench seating. The pictured Lone Star has Deluxe Cloth Bucket Seat upholstery and power adjustment. The pictured Laramie has Leather-Trimmed Bucket Seats. These are exact seating configurations, not every cloth or leather interior. Other equipment in the picture is not selected automatically.

questions.title: Would you like a panoramic sunroof?
questions.explanation: Swipe this roof photo right to require a panoramic sunroof, or left to exclude it. No preference keeps either choice.
questions.availability: R12315’s original sticker lists its Dual-Pane Panoramic Sunroof in OPTIONAL EQUIPMENT. This is an installed option on the pictured Laramie, not a claim that every Laramie includes it. The panoramic glass roof replaces the conventional roof configuration. A verified photo of the alternative roof is not yet in this guide.

questions.title: How do you want to adjust your seat?
questions.explanation: Compare the actual seat controls. Power adjustment replaces the manual adjustment mechanism; lumbar support and memory are separate features.
questions.availability: R12196’s sticker lists a 4-Way Manual Adjustable Driver Seat. R12527’s sticker confirms an 8-Way Power Adjustable Driver Seat. These are the installed configurations shown in the photos. The power seat changes the adjustment mechanism, not just the seating material. Trim and package combinations vary; the exact number of adjustments follows each VIN’s sticker.

questions.title: Which dashboard screen do you want?
questions.explanation: The larger center screen replaces the smaller center-screen system. These photos show the screens installed in two different Ram 3500 dashboards.
questions.availability: R12500 has the optional 12-inch system in its Tradesman Level 2A Equipment Group, replacing its standard 8.4-inch screen. The 12-inch system is standard on Laramie. The larger UBW system is a Laramie package option and standard on Limited/Longhorn. The factory chart calls UBW 14.5 inches; the manufacturer bulletin identifies UBW as 14.4 inches. The pictured used R12249A sticker lists 14.4 inches as standard, and inventory matching retains that exact size. Select Used or Both to include this pictured truck. Its sticker describes the original build; confirm current equipment before purchase.

questions.title: Which front-seat configuration do you want?
questions.explanation: These choices match the exact seating configurations printed on the pictured trucks’ stickers. The bench is shown with its center backrest folded down; bucket seats have a separate full-length center console. Other materials and layouts remain available through No preference.
questions.availability: Vinyl bench seating is standard on Tradesman. Laramie starts with a leather-trimmed bench; bucket seats are an optional replacement, included with qualifying packages. Pictured R12512 lists its leather-trimmed buckets inside the optional Laramie Level 1 Plus Equipment Group. Heating, ventilation and power adjustment are separate features.

questions.title: Which seat upholstery do you prefer?
questions.explanation: Choose between these two actual interiors. Nappa leather-trimmed seating replaces the Caprice leatherette upholstery when moving from Select to Limited. Seat heating, ventilation and power adjustment are separate features.
questions.availability: The 2026 factory guide lists Caprice leatherette-trimmed buckets as standard on Select and Nappa leather-trimmed buckets as standard on Limited. The pictured C02225 Select sticker says Caprice Leatherette Bucket Seats; the pictured P04984 Limited sticker says Nappa Leather Bucket Seats. P04984 is a used vehicle. Only the labeled upholstery is selected, not every feature visible in the photo.

questions.title: Would you like this panoramic sunroof?
questions.explanation: Swipe this actual roof photo right to require a panoramic sunroof or left to exclude it. No preference keeps either configuration. The panoramic glass roof replaces the conventional roof configuration.
questions.availability: C02225’s original sticker lists its Dual-Pane Panoramic Sunroof and Power Open / Close Shade under OPTIONAL EQUIPMENT. It is an installed option on this pictured Select. The 2026 factory guide lists the dual-pane panoramic roof as standard on Limited and Pinnacle; P04984’s Limited sticker also lists it in standard equipment. A verified photo of the conventional roof is not yet available in this guide.

questions.title: Which dashboard screen do you want?
questions.explanation: The larger center touchscreen replaces the smaller center touchscreen. These images show the actual installed screens in two verified 2026 Grand Cherokee vehicles.
questions.availability: Laredo J22581 has an 8.4-inch Uconnect 5 touchscreen. Limited J22138 has a 12.3-inch Uconnect 5 Nav touchscreen. The separate passenger display is a different feature.

questions.title: Which seating material do you want?
questions.explanation: Cloth, Capri leatherette and Palermo leather are different seat coverings. Leatherette is a synthetic material. Choosing one replaces the previous seat covering.
questions.availability: These exact factory upholstery descriptions come from the pictured Laredo, Limited and Summit vehicles. Upholstery selection does not automatically select the pictured interior color or every feature visible around the seats.

questions.title: Would you like a panoramic sunroof?
questions.explanation: The panoramic glass roof replaces the conventional roof configuration. It is different from the smaller single-pane sunroof available on some trims.
questions.availability: The pictured Summit includes the dual-pane panoramic sunroof. The verified trim path explains where this roof is included or optional; a single-pane roof is not treated as the same feature.

questions.title: Which front-seat covering do you want?
questions.explanation: The photos show actual Sport cloth and Rubicon Nappa leather seats. Nappa leather replaces cloth; choosing the covering does not select the pictured paint color or roof.
questions.availability: Sport-style cloth and Rubicon Nappa leather are different factory seating configurations. Rubicon cloth uses a different seat code and is not represented by the Sport photo. Choosing the covering does not select every pictured seat feature. The original dealer banners remain; this guide does not select a promotional offer.

questions.title: Which roof system do you want?
questions.explanation: A removable 3-piece hardtop and the Sky One-Touch power top are different installed roof systems. The Sky One-Touch image shows its fabric section retracted.
questions.availability: Sport starts with a Black Sunrider soft top. These photos show the removable hardtop and Sky One-Touch upgrades. Use No preference to leave the roof open. Roof color and other pictured features are not selected automatically.
